text:
deploy-bot: Deploy started for inference-api v2.3.0 -> canary 5% (region: us-east-1) at 1900123456

sam (oncall): ack

maria (eng): watching canary logs/metrics, will check heartbeat panel

ops-bot: metric alert fired: `canary_heartbeat_missing` for inference-api-canary (threshold 2m)

elliot (sre): I see the alert too — paging oncall. pagerduty: @sam

incident-bot: Paging sam (oncall) — high-severity: canary heartbeat missing (inference-api)

sam (oncall): on it. what does "heartbeat" mean here? is this the k8s readiness ping or our synthetic request?

maria (eng): it should be the synthetic heartbeat probe from canary-runner hitting /healthz once every 30s. grafana panel normally shows last 5m of pings. I'm not seeing that panel open rn

sam (oncall): grafana dashboard link?

maria (eng): https://grafana.internal/d/infra/canary-health  — when I open it it's 404. maybe renamed during the docs cleanup last week :/

tina (prodops): ugh. we did a dashboard tidy yesterday, might have removed that panel accidentally. investigating who edited it.

sam (oncall): without the panel we only have alerts. is there evidence customers impacted? alex-cs pinged earlier about slow replies from a customer sandbox

alex-cs: yes customer reported intermittent request timeouts ~14:03-14:10. unsure if related to canary. they said they saw 500s from inference-api

maria (eng): checking canary pods: logs show synthetic runner failing to bind socket with `EADDRINUSE` for the short period after rollout started. looks like new sidecar changed port allocation?

elliot (sre): that could cause heartbeat failures. do we have SLO burn alarms firing?

ops-bot: SLO alert: inference-api_p99_latency > 2s (5m window) — but it's flapping on/off.

sam (oncall): ok we have three converging signals: heartbeat missing, pod error in canary, customer timeouts, SLO flapping. recommend kill the feature flag for v2.3.0 canary routing to stop new canaries. @maria can you flip?

maria (eng): prepping kill now. running:```bash
# disable canary routing
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $FLAG_TOKEN" \
  https://flags.internal/api/flags/inference-api_canary -d '{"state":"off"}'
```

maria (eng): done — response 200. canary routing disabled.

deploy-bot: Canary traffic scaled down to 0% for inference-api v2.3.0

sam (oncall): nice. monitor SLOs and customer reports. do we need a rollback?

maria (eng): since we only hit canary, no full rollback required. root cause looks like a sidecar port collision introduced by a change in the init script. I'll open a PR to revert the sidecar change.

alex-cs: told customer we disabled canary and are investigating. they asked for ETA — told them ~1h for root cause + fix PR, longer for full rollout resume.

elliot (sre): we still have noisy alerts for `canary_heartbeat_missing` since dashboard missing. can we suppress duplicates and annotate incident?

sam (oncall): set alert to maintenance for 30m?

tina (prodops): putting the alert into silence window for 40m now — reason: canary removal in progress — ticket #INC-4621

maria (eng): FYI the grafana panel was accidentally deleted (editor: ops-dashbot) — I'm restoring it from snapshot, but snapshot includes old panel id so queries need minor edits (metric name changed last month).

ops-bot: restored panel draft at /d/infra/canary-health?panel=restore-1900123456 — pending validation

sam (oncall): good. once panel is back, we should switch alert to reference that panel timerule instead of the generic metric so we reduce noise.

maria (eng): agreed. also adding an explicit canary readiness metric emitted by the runner to avoid sidecar-port entanglement. PR coming in 20m.

elliot (sre): handoff note for next oncall (sam -> tina in 30m): incident: canary heartbeat missing during v2.3.0 canary. mitigated by disabling canary routing. customer reported transient 500s; follow up needed to confirm no residual impact. alerts silenced temporarily. dashboards restored draft. files: #INC-4621

sam (oncall): copying that to the rotation channel. @tina you'll take next 12h if anything else flares.

tina (prodops): taking it. thanks. I'll watch for any more paging and coordinate postmortem doc.

maria (eng): small postmortem plan: timeline + root cause (sidecar init change), impact (canary only, one customer transient errors), mitigation (disabled canary, silence alerts), follow-ups (revert sidecar change, re-add robust canary heartbeat metric, dashboard guardrail). PR/PMs looped.

sam (oncall): thanks team. quick note: create a short runbook step for toggling canary via flag in case this happens again — include curl snippet above and who to page.

alex-cs: customer acknowledged the update and will re-test later. they asked to be notified when rollout resumes.

ops-bot: Incident closed for paging reasons — no active pages pending. please file postmortem in #incidents and link here. :white_check_mark:

sam (oncall): closing thread summary: canary heartbeat alert triggered due to sidecar port collision after dashboard panel had been removed. mitigated by disabling canary routing and silencing related alerts. next: revert sidecar change, add explicit heartbeat metric, harden dashboard guardrails.

maria (eng): PR opened: https://git.internal/p/inference/merge-1423 — tag: revert-sidecar-port — will request review

tina (prodops): I'll draft the postmortem and ask cs to confirm customer status before reopen.

elliot (sre): leaving a short note for alerting team: add an integration test to ensure critical dashboard panels are not deleted by the cleanup script — open ticket #ALERT-808

sam (oncall): thanks all. moving to monitoring mode.
